analysis: The supplied units are BASE-side text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (base lines 4074-4930). The only changed base lines per the range map are 3, 3635 and 4030, which fall outside these excerpts. The head-side additions (the Gemma 4 tensor-parallel foundation section and the ClusterTensorParallelChoice.fastest placement text) are only partially visible in the truncated patch excerpt, so I could not review them fully. This PR is documentation-only, with no source, config or runtime change in the supplied evidence, so I found no concrete security regression. The excerpt describes pre-existing cluster behavior: bounded authenticated-record transport, fail-closed refusal on data-plane failure instead of raw fallback, and load-agreement binding of KV and SSD-prefix precision. It also covers encrypted SSD prefix records bound by directory, header encoding and agreement, with fail-closed deletion and recompute on mismatch. The related threat is T-041 (prefix cache, SSD at rest, TTFT oracle), and the described controls match its mitigations: HMAC-keyed names, sealed headers and a refusal path for foreign encodings. Nothing here widens the at-rest surface or changes TTL or salt scoping. The claims about lossy restored rows and mixed exact/approximate ranks are documented as accepted correctness tradeoffs, not confidentiality changes. Remaining question: the new Gemma 4 TP section and any cluster tensor-parallel placement or agreement changes sit in head-side hunks outside these units. Integration should check whether they add transport or prefix-record surfaces (TB-002 and TB-007 analogues) or alter T-041 assumptions. Unverified: the doc's claims about the code, since no source was supplied.
